description: Follow the path from a drawing call to lit pixels on an OLED, and compare the state before and after show().

educational.topic: Framebuffer drawing and the show() command
learningObjectives: Explain the path from a drawing call to lit pixels on the OLED
Distinguish what changes before show() from what changes after show()
State how many bytes cross the bus on each show()

keyQuestions: Why is drawing into RAM faster than drawing on the display?
Why should show() be called once per frame?
What does the SSD1306 do if the Pico stops sending data?
commonMisconceptions: oled.text() draws directly on the screen (it changes the RAM buffer)
show() only sends the pixels that changed (it sends the whole buffer)
assessmentOpportunities: The student explains that drawing calls change only RAM.
The student states that show() sends all 1,024 bytes every time.
The student diagnoses a missing show() call from its symptom.
